title: Back pay and continuity can be implemented while actual workplace return remains unresolved
source_unit: Fair Work Commission Full Bench decision [2015] FWCFB 1523 concerning Sportsmed SA and Cartisano
geography: South Australia; Fair Work Commission Sportsmed SA appeal

observations.period: November 2013 through June 24, 2015; injury, dismissal, remedy payment, risk-assessment exclusion, unconditional reinstatement, and disputed altered return

work_and_injury.value: The worker suffered a non-work-related motor-vehicle injury, returned with restrictions, stopped working, and was terminated from a CSSD Manager role on November 7, 2013; the Commission found the dismissal unfair

remedy_payment.value: Sportsmed reported payment of back pay owing under the order on or about August 14, 2014 and wages for a further two weeks, with continuity maintained

practical_access.value: The worker was not permitted to return while a medical/risk assessment was undertaken and was treated as on unpaid leave; the Full Bench held the conditional order did not achieve actual reinstatement and issued separate unconditional reinstatement order PR561823

later_return.value: A later public court record reports return on March 26, 2015, materially altered duties and status, and cessation of work on June 24, 2015 while still employed; final remedy and later livelihood remain unobserved

mechanism.value: Payment and legal continuity are distinct remedy currencies from actual access to the workplace; a risk-assessment process can leave a worker without practical return even after monetary implementation

observations.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission Full Bench decision, reinstatement order, and public later court record; back-pay payment, conditional exclusion, legal correction, and disputed later return are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: Private medical, payroll, household, treatment, alternative-job, and later-employment records are not retained. Exact net payment, final remedy execution, whether altered duties satisfied the order, and post-decision livelihood are not independently established.
observations.subgroup: One publicly adjudicated worker with injury-related work restrictions and a disputed reinstatement route; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: The employer's risk assessment may have reflected genuine safety concerns, and a later altered role or cessation may have multiple causes; payment and continuity do not by themselves prove either exclusion or recovery.

related_sources.claim: Public later court record reports a March 2015 return, materially altered duties, cessation while still employed, and unresolved constructive-reinstatement dispute.

boundary: This record establishes a same-case boundary in which reported back-pay payment and continuity coexist with no actual return, and the tribunal distinguishes legal payment from real and practical reinstatement. It does not establish final remedy, causality of non-return, later compensation, household recovery, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the public FWC and follow-up court records; private medical, payroll, household, and employment files are not retained.
